commands.name: status
commands.description: Status for the active part: id, name, editor script, runState (not_run_yet | ok | failed), and the last run volume/bbox/bodyCount when available. Updates when the active part changes without requiring another run. featureCount counts insert_* feature blocks, so a freehand set_script is one feature. bodyCount is null until the first run; a finished run that produced no bodies reports 0.

commands.name: errors
commands.description: Structured errors from the last finished geometry run. message is the same text the viewport shows. featureType, featureLabel, and featureIndex identify the failed feature when known. detail is the exception name, a Manifold status, or the kernel message when that text is not already in message. Stack frames and URLs are omitted, and detail is always present on feature_failed: when the kernel adds nothing, it names the helper that threw (move adds how to name the body). Cleared on the next successful run. Feature and kernel failures use code feature_failed. A geometry engine crash (a wasm abort, out of memory, or a run past its time budget) is one row with code geometry_worker_crashed, reason (wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost), and workerRestarted: the worker was replaced, other parts kept building, and the next run of this part uses the fresh worker; simplify the part, reduce segment counts, or split it up. No reload is needed.

commands.name: screenshot
commands.description: Capture the viewport, centered on the camera target (an open feature card's view offset is not applied to the capture). The default is a full-size PNG data URL. Optional max_width and scale downscale in the browser before encoding. format is png or jpeg; quality (0 to 1) applies to jpeg only.

format.description: Image format. Omit for png, the historical default. jpeg is smaller.

quality.description: jpeg quality from 0 to 1. Ignored for png. Default 0.8.

max_width.description: Downscale in the browser so the width is at most this many pixels. Does not upscale.

scale.description: Multiply width and height by this factor (0 exclusive to 1). Applied before max_width. Does not upscale.

commands.name: undo
commands.description: One undo on the feature-bar stack (sketch session, assembly joints, or active part script) and run when the part script changes. A part step returns the refreshed status, bodyCount included.

commands.name: redo

commands.name: history
commands.description: Summary of the stack the next undo/redo would use: entries, head, labels, canUndo, canRedo.

commands.description: Toggle operator-visible cues (synthetic cursor, highlights, pacing).

enabled.description: Turn operator-visible cues on or off

commands.name: feature_tree
commands.description: Feature strip for the active part script.

commands.name: selection
commands.description: Current viewport and editor selection summary.

commands.name: mode
commands.description: Open picker / card mode summary. featureEdit is { mode, featureId, kind, dialog } while any feature edit is open (the App sheet or the viewport card open_feature put up), else null.

commands.name: dirty
commands.description: Working-copy dirty flags. unsaved is true when the WC differs from the last AssemblyCommit (survives reload; covers rename, hide, and remove). pendingSave is an offline planned write waiting for a second Save. Changing activeId does not set assemblyDirty.

commands.name: toasts
commands.description: Visible upload / git / rename notices.

commands.name: parts
commands.description: Open assembly: assemblyId, assemblyName, vaultLayout, activeId, and parts [{ id, name, visible, missing?, group?, runState, crash? }]. runState is not_run_yet | ok | failed for every part, not only the active one; crash is present after a geometry engine crash on that part ({ code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason, workerRestarted, message }). Part and assembly ids are opaque surf ids, never a path or display name. No path field. featureCount and bodyCount are on status, not here. featureCount counts insert_* feature blocks, so a freehand set_script is one feature. bodyCount is null until the first run; a finished run that produced no bodies reports 0.

commands.name: camera
commands.description: Current camera pose.

commands.name: list_faces
commands.description: Every pickable face on the active part, or on part_id when set (an opaque surf id, never a path or display name). One row per face a viewport click selects, all bodies: id (f0, f1, …), type (planar, cylindrical, curved), center, normal, axis and radius for cylinders, area, and key. The id is the patch index on this mesh and is only valid until the next remesh; a rerun of the same script keeps every id. Pass the key with the id to joint_pick so a stale id cannot silently pick another face.

commands.name: list_bodies
commands.description: Bodies of the active part's last run, in mesh order: [{ index, at, triangleCount }]. index is insert_move body_index; at is the centroid move() names (insert_move at, edit_feature at). Empty before the first run.

commands.name: geometry_workers
commands.description: Debug status of the geometry workers: cap (workers this device gets, the primary included: min(cores − 1, GB of deviceMemory), 1..4 on a phone, 1..8 on a desktop; the dev override is ?geometryWorkers=N or localStorage surfcadGeometryWorkers), live, busy, queued, peakBusy, crashes, primary { ready, busy, jobs, heapMB, crashes, lastCrash }, and pool { size, live, busy, queued, peakBusy, jobsDone, jobsFailed, members: [{ id, live, busy, jobs, heapMB, recycled, crashes }] }. The parts that are not active build on the pool, several at once; the active part, cross-sections, and previews use the primary. Read-only.
